extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, and attorneys facing or advising on reciprocal discipline
extracted.subtask_description: Formal Final Order imposing suspension from practice before the USPTO under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, describing basis for reciprocal discipline, procedural requirements, enforcement mechanisms, publication/notice obligations, and conditions for reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension term and reinstatement eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the Office for a period of thirty-six (36) months (paragraph (a)). Respondent is granted the right to seek reinstatement after serving twelve (12) months of his suspension (paragraph (h)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension begins on the date of the Final Order. A petition for reinstatement may be filed any time after 12 months from the date the Final Order is signed and prior to the expiration of the 36‑month suspension period. If not reinstated within 36 months, there is no remaining period of suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis for discipline — reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The suspension is based on Respondent's violation of the Disciplinary Rule set forth in 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(5), and was requested as reciprocal discipline under a Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 (introductory paragraphs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reciprocal discipline may be imposed when a practitioner has been suspended by a state disciplinary authority for ethical grounds; the Notice and Order informed Respondent the OED Director filed a Complaint requesting reciprocal discipline based on the State Bar of Texas suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to file a timely response to contest imposition
rubrics_metrics.description: If Respondent seeks to contest imposition of suspension pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d), Respondent shall file within forty (40) days a response containing all information Respondent believes is sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact that identical discipline would be unwarranted under the grounds permissible under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1) (Notice and Order description).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The response must contain all information supporting any of the specific grounds listed in §11.24(d)(1); failure to timely respond may result in a determination that no genuine issue of material fact exists and imposition of the requested discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service by publication when mail is returned
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Notice and Order mailing is returned (e.g., Post Office Box closed with no forwarding address), service by publication is authorized pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(b) and 11.35(b) and was effected by publication in the Official Gazette (Notice and Order paragraphs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication in the Official Gazette constitutes notice when direct mail service cannot be accomplished; Respondent may obtain copies by written request to the USPTO General Counsel as indicated in the published notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 while suspended
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 while suspended (paragraph (b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §11.58 contains the practitioner's duties while suspended (e.g., notice obligations and handling of client matters). The Final Order also grants limited recognition to practice for thirty (30) days solely to facilitate compliance with §11.58(b) (paragraph (c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition to facilitate compliance with § 11.58(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is granted limited recognition to practice before the Office beginning on the date this Final Order is signed and expiring thirty (30) days after the date this Final Order is signed for the sole purpose of facilitating Respondent's compliance with the provisions of 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b) (paragraph (c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This narrow, time-limited recognition permits actions necessary only to meet §11.58(b) requirements (e.g., communications/filings to wind down or transition client matters) and expires after 30 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from USPTO customer numbers and PKI certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall promptly dissociate Respondent's name from all USPTO customer numbers and public key infrastructure ("PKI") certificates (paragraph (d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent shall not use any USPTO customer number or PKI certificate unless and until reinstated, and shall not obtain a new customer number or PKI certificate until reinstated (paragraphs (e) and (f)). These steps are to prevent practice before the Office during suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall remain suspended until the OED Director grants a petition requesting reinstatement based upon Respondent showing proof to the satisfaction of the OED Director that: (1) Respondent has the good moral character and reputation, competency, and learning in law required under 37 C.F.R. § 11.7 for admission; (2) resumption of Respondent's practice before the Office will not be detrimental to the administration of justice or subversive to the public interest; and (3) Respondent has complied with the provisions of 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 for the full period of suspension (paragraph (g)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement is discretionary and requires clear proof on all three prongs to the satisfaction of the OED Director per §11.60(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and mechanics of petition for reinstatement and stay of remaining suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent may file a petition for reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 at any time after twelve (12) months from the date this Final Order is signed and prior to expiration of the 36‑month suspension (paragraph (h)). The OED Director shall stay any remaining period of suspension if the OED Director grants a petition requesting Respondent's immediate reinstatement and reinstates Respondent (paragraph (i)). The term "remaining period of suspension" is defined as the 36‑month initial suspension minus the time served until reinstatement; if not reinstated prior to 36 months, there is no remaining period (paragraph (j)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A successful reinstatement petition can result in staying the unserved portion of the suspension; if reinstatement is denied or later undone, the remaining suspension may be imposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED Director authority to issue Order to Show Cause for noncompliance during suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director is of the opinion that Respondent failed to comply with any provision of the Final Order or any Disciplinary Rule during the 36‑month period, the OED Director shall (1) issue to Respondent an Order to Show Cause and (2) send it to Respondent at the last address of record and grant Respondent fifteen (15) days to respond (paragraph (k)(1)(A)–(C)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are two branches: (i) if Respondent has not yet been reinstated, the OED Director may seek to amend the Final Order to require waiting until full 36 months before filing for reinstatement; (ii) if Respondent has been reinstated and a stay exists, OED may seek lifting the stay and immediate suspension for all or part of the remaining period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-Show-Cause procedure and referral to USPTO Director
rubrics_metrics.description: After the 15‑day response period, if the OED Director continues to be of that opinion, the OED Director shall deliver to the USPTO Director: (i) the Order to Show Cause, (ii) Respondent's response, if any, and (iii) evidence supporting the OED Director's opinion; and request that the USPTO Director either amend the Final Order to delay reinstatement eligibility or lift the stay and immediately suspend for the remaining period (paragraph (k)(2)(A)–(B)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the formal escalation mechanism from OED to the USPTO Director to enforce compliance and alter reinstatement eligibility or stay status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences if suspended pursuant to an amended order under paragraph (k)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Respondent is suspended pursuant to the provisions of paragraph (k), Respondent shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58; the OED Director shall disseminate information in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59; the USPTO shall dissociate Respondent's name from customer numbers and PKI certificates; Respondent shall not use or obtain customer numbers or PKI certificates unless reinstated (paragraph (l)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The same administrative safeguards and publication obligations apply if the OED/USPTO imposes or reinstates suspension under enforcement provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeated enforcement actions permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Final Order shall limit the number of times the OED Director or the USPTO Director may act pursuant to paragraph (k) for acts and/or omissions occurring during the 36‑month period commencing on the date the Final Order is signed (paragraph (m)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED/USPTO may repeatedly pursue enforcement actions for separate or continuing noncompliance during the suspension period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of seeking review on immediate suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: If Respondent seeks a review of the USPTO Director's action (e.g., amending the Final Order or lifting a stay), any such review shall not operate to postpone or otherwise hold in abeyance the Director's order (paragraphs (n) and (s)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative or judicial review does not stay the suspension or other immediate enforcement steps taken by the Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office may seek additional discipline under §§ 11.34–11.57
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Final Order shall prevent the Office from seeking discipline against Respondent in accordance with the provisions of 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.34 through 11.57 for the misconduct upon which an Order to Show Cause is issued by the OED Director under paragraph (k) (paragraph (t)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate or additional proceedings under the Code of Professional Responsibility procedures may be pursued for the same misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish this Final Order (paragraph (p)). The OED Director shall publish a Notice of Suspension in the Official Gazette and disseminate notice of the public discipline and reasons for discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the State where the practitioner is admitted to practice, to courts where the practitioner is known to be admitted, and to the public in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 (paragraphs (q) and (r)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice of Suspension includes identifying information, the regulatory basis for discipline, eligibility to request reinstatement after 12 months subject to conditions, and a brief description of the underlying state-bar misconduct. Disciplinary decisions are also posted in OED Reading Room for public access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the disciplinary record in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The record of this disciplinary proceeding, including this Final Order, shall be considered (1) when addressing any further complaint or evidence of the same or similar misconduct brought to the attention of the Office, and/or (2) in any future disciplinary proceeding as an aggravating factor and/or to rebut any statement or representation by or on Respondent's behalf (paragraph (u)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior disciplinary records can be used to increase sanctions or to challenge representations made by the respondent in future matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of misconduct underlying the state suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: Mr. Black was suspended from the practice of law in Texas for a period of three years for: (1) neglecting a legal matter entrusted to him; (2) failing to carry out completely the obligations that the lawyer owes to a client or clients; (3) failing to keep a client reasonably informed about the status of a matter and promptly comply with reasonable requests for information; (4) failing to explain a matter to the extent reasonably necessary to permit a client to make informed decisions regarding the representation; and (5) entering into a business transaction with a client wherein the transaction and terms on which the lawyer acquired the interest were unfair and unreasonable to the client and were not fully disclosed in a manner which could be reasonably understood by the client (Notice of Suspension text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These specific types of misconduct, as found by the State Bar, were the factual basis for the reciprocal discipline; similar misconduct may warrant equivalent consideration by OED/USPTO in future cases.
